prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2015 – summary (under 500 words)

Core vision
- Build a strong economy as the foundation for opportunity and secure public services at every life stage.
- Protect and improve the NHS; reward work; back enterprise; strengthen national security; keep the Union together; let voters decide on EU membership.

Economy, tax and welfare
- Eliminate the deficit, run a surplus, keep debt falling; no rises in VAT, Income Tax or National Insurance.
- Raise the Personal Allowance to £12,500 and the 40p threshold to £50,000; new “Tax‑Free Minimum Wage” link.
- Crack down on tax avoidance/evasion; permanent Office of Tax Simplification.
- Welfare: lower household benefit cap to £23,000; freeze most working-age benefits for two years; roll out Universal Credit; tougher youth benefit rules; expand childcare (30 hours free for working parents of 3–4 year‑olds) and tax‑free childcare.

Jobs, business and infrastructure
- Aim for full employment; create 2 million more jobs and 3 million apprenticeships; abolish long‑term youth unemployment.
- Keep a competitive business tax regime; cut £10bn of red tape; late payment measures; start‑up loans expansion.
- Major infrastructure: >£100bn capital plan; HS2/HS3, rail electrification, roads investment, real‑terms freeze on regulated commuter fares; superfast broadband to 95% by 2017; extend mobile coverage and lead on 5G.
- Regional growth: Northern Powerhouse; devolved powers and elected mayors; local business rates retention pilots.

Education and skills
- Protect per‑pupil funding; tougher primary standards and resits if needed; core academic GCSEs.
- Turn all failing and “coasting” schools into academies; at least 500 new free schools.
- Expand teacher recruitment (maths/physics/Mandarin) and reduce bureaucracy.
- No cap on university places; new postgraduate loans; more Degree Apprenticeships; strengthen FE and UTCs.

Health and care
- Increase NHS funding in real terms, with at least £8bn extra by 2020; deliver a 7‑day NHS and GP access (same‑day for over‑75s).
- Integrate health and social care via Better Care Fund; cancer strategy, mental health parity and waiting standards; electronic health records and transparency.
- Cap residential social care costs; more support for carers; dementia strategy.

Housing
- Double first‑time buyers; extend Help to Buy and launch Help to Buy ISA.
- Build 200,000 Starter Homes (20% discount for under‑40 first‑time buyers); 275,000 additional affordable homes.
- Extend Right to Buy to housing association tenants; prioritise brownfield; protect Green Belt.

Immigration and security
- Target net migration in the tens of thousands; EU welfare restrictions (four‑year rule), end jobseeker benefits; stronger enforcement, landlord checks, illegal working clampdown; English fluency for public‑facing roles.
- Counter‑terrorism: new communications data law; powers against extremist groups/individuals; tackle online radicalisation.

Law, order and rights
- Continue police reform; focus on cyber‑crime; modernise prisons and expand rehabilitation; Victims’ Law; stronger action on violence against women and girls.
- Scrap the Human Rights Act; introduce a British Bill of Rights.

Energy and environment
- Keep bills down via competition and smart meters; insulate 1m more homes.
- Back new nuclear, gas, offshore wind; end new subsidies for onshore wind; support shale with community benefits.
- 25‑year nature plan; protect Green Belt and forests; “Blue Belt” for marine habitats; flood defences.

Pensions and inheritance
- Keep the triple lock; introduce single‑tier pension; protect pensioner benefits; pension freedoms and tax‑free inheritance of pots; raise effective Inheritance Tax threshold on family homes to £1m for couples.

Union, Europe, and foreign policy
- English votes for English laws (including on Income Tax); implement new powers for Scotland and Wales; sustain Northern Ireland settlement.
- EU: renegotiate and hold an in‑out referendum by end‑2017; keep the pound; protect Single Market; cut EU red tape.
- Defence: maintain strong Armed Forces, renew Trident, invest in equipment; meet global challenges with diplomacy and 0.7% aid, focusing on poverty, health, girls’ education and humanitarian crises.
